title: Jalan Alor Food Street: What to Eat and When to Go
metaDescription: Jalan Alor food street in Bukit Bintang: what to eat, when the night market gets busy, halal and cash tips, and how to get there from KLIA2.

contentBlocks.content: Jalan Alor food street is one strip just off Bukit Bintang where hawker stalls and open-fronted restaurants line both sides and tables spill onto the road after sunset (Malaysia Taste). It is the place most visitors mean when they ask about Jalan Alor food or the Jalan Alor night market. This guide covers where it is, when to go, what to order, how halal works on a mixed street, and how to get there from KLIA2. For the wider area, see the Bukit Bintang food guide.
Key Takeaways
Where is Jalan Alor? In Bukit Bintang, about a five minute walk from Bukit Bintang station on the MRT and Monorail (Malaysia Taste).
When should I go? In the evening. CK Travels, writing in October 2023, found stalls setting up from around 4.30pm to 5.30pm and closing around midnight to 1am, later at weekends (CK Travels).
What do I eat first? Satay, char kway teow, grilled seafood and charcoal grilled chicken wings, then cendol or putu piring for dessert (Tourism Malaysia, Malaysia Taste).
Is it halal? Not as a whole. Many stalls serve or cook with pork, so look for a halal certificate or ask at each stall (Malaysia Taste).
Do I need cash? Bring small notes. Cards and e-wallets are not accepted everywhere (Malaysia Taste).
Where Jalan Alor is

Jalan Alor sits in Bukit Bintang, an easy walk from Pavilion, Lot 10 and Fahrenheit 88 (Malaysia Taste). Take the MRT or the Monorail to Bukit Bintang station, near Lot 10, and walk about five minutes. On the MRT, CK Travels used exit F (CK Travels). The street runs for about 500 metres with around 200 stalls and restaurants (CK Travels).

Changkat Bukit Bintang, the bar street, is within a ten minute walk (CK Travels). Coming by Grab? Ask to be dropped at either end, because cars crawl through the middle in the evening (Malaysia Taste).
Before you fly, save Bukit Bintang station in your map app so you can walk straight there after check-in.
When to go: Jalan Alor night market hours

The permanent restaurants open from lunchtime, but the street is quiet in the day. CK Travels, writing in October 2023, found the night market stalls setting up from around 4.30pm to 5.30pm and usually closing around midnight to 1am, with many staying open later at weekends. Each stall keeps its own hours (CK Travels).

Between 5.30pm and 7pm you can walk the street before the crowds. From 7pm to 10pm it is in full swing, and walking the 500 metres can be slow (CK Travels). Malaysia Taste suggests arriving around 6.30pm or 7pm, when most stalls are running (Malaysia Taste).

KL often gets heavy showers in the late afternoon or evening. Wait under an awning or in a nearby mall, then go back out (Malaysia Taste). Plan your first visit for about 6.30pm and give yourself two hours.
What to eat on Jalan Alor

Tourism Malaysia lists nasi goreng, laksa and satay as staples here. It names Restoran Wong Ah Wah for barbecued chicken wings smoked over a charcoal grill, Boleh Seafood Pot for a hot seafood soup, and a putu piring stall serving steamed rice cake with grated coconut and gula Melaka. Durian and other local fruit are sold on the pavement (Tourism Malaysia).

Malaysia Taste starts first-timers on char kway teow, satay, grilled squid or stingray, fried oyster omelette, and cendol, ais kacang or tau fu fa to finish (Malaysia Taste). CK Travels also found lok lok, dim sum, apam balik and coconut ice cream (CK Travels).

The Teeko directory lists the street itself. Expect satay, grilled seafood, chicken wings, beef skewers, noodle dishes and fried snacks from open-air stalls under neon lights, and plenty of people out for supper.
Meng Kee Grill Fish is at 39 Jalan Alor. It cooks seafood and grilled dishes over an open flame, and it suits a late meal with cold drinks.
Order small portions at several places rather than a full meal at one. You will cover far more of the street that way (Malaysia Taste).
Halal food on Jalan Alor

Jalan Alor is a mixed street. Many stalls serve pork or cook with it, so it is not a halal food street. Look for a halal certificate at the stall or ask before you order. Do not assume a chicken or seafood dish is halal just because there is no pork in it (Malaysia Taste).
Alcohol is sold at the sit-down restaurants, not at the street stalls (CK Travels). If you eat halal, ask at each stall, and keep the mall food courts around Bukit Bintang as a backup.
Practical tips before you sit down

Carry small notes. Many stalls still prefer cash, and cards and e-wallets are not accepted everywhere (Malaysia Taste). Bring tissues or wet wipes too, because plenty of stalls do not hand out napkins (Malaysia Taste).
Seafood is often priced by weight. Ask the price before it goes on the grill (Malaysia Taste). Sit at the tables that belong to the stall you order from (Malaysia Taste).
Restaurant staff will hold out menus as you pass. Smile and keep walking if you are not interested. At weekends the ends of the street get crowded, so watch your phone and wallet (CK Travels).
Walk the whole street once before you choose, and pick the stalls with a queue and fast turnover.
More to eat and do nearby

Jalan Alor is one part of a larger food area. The Bukit Bintang food guide covers Lot 10 Hutong, Pavilion and the vegan kitchens nearby. Still hungry at midnight? The supper in Kuala Lumpur guide lists more late spots. For the day before dinner, read things to do in Bukit Bintang.
Getting to Jalan Alor from KLIA2

The bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC ends in Bukit Bintang City Centre. From there the Monorail runs two stops, through Imbi, to Bukit Bintang, and Jalan Alor is a short walk from the station. The fare is shown on the booking page. The KLIA2 to Bukit Bintang guide compares every option, and the Lalaport BBCC guide explains the hub.

Frequently Asked Questions
Is Jalan Alor food halal?
Jalan Alor food is not halal as a whole. Many stalls serve or cook with pork. Look for a halal certificate or ask at each stall before you order (Malaysia Taste).
What time does Jalan Alor open?

Jalan Alor restaurants open from lunchtime. CK Travels, writing in October 2023, found the night market stalls setting up from around 4.30pm to 5.30pm and closing around midnight to 1am, later at weekends (CK Travels).
How do I get to Jalan Alor by train?
To get to Jalan Alor by train, take the MRT or the Monorail to Bukit Bintang station and walk about five minutes (Malaysia Taste).
Do Jalan Alor stalls take cards?
Some Jalan Alor stalls take cards or e-wallets, but many still prefer cash. Bring small notes (Malaysia Taste).
Can you drink beer on Jalan Alor?
Yes, at the sit-down restaurants on Jalan Alor. The street stalls do not sell alcohol (CK Travels).
Conclusion

Jalan Alor food street is at its liveliest from early evening, a five minute walk from Bukit Bintang station. Bring small notes, ask about pork at each stall, and share plates as you go. Landing at KLIA2? Book the bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC on ttklia.com and have dinner on Jalan Alor tonight.
